# Drawing sheet template (Revit)

The Broadsheet drawing sheet: an Arch D (36 x 24 in) sheet with a title strip down the right edge, built in Revit
(tested on 2026; the scripts read the running Revit's own family and project templates) through `bim revit exec`. Published with the kit from 0.6.3 on at
`https://ui.bimisland.com/kit/<version>/templates/sheet/`.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `sheet.json` | The source: sheet size, strip rows, text styles, static words, per-sheet fields, and one block per property (wordmark, URL, tagline, disclaimer, family and template names). Colours are kit token names (`text`, `muted`) or `spot`; faces are kit roles (`serif-700`, `sans-400`, `sans-600`, `mono-400`). |
| `sheet.<property>.json` | GENERATED by `scripts/gen-sheet.mjs` (`pnpm --filter @bim-pdf/ui-kit gen`): the same layout with concrete Revit fonts and rgb from DESIGN.md (light theme, the property's light spot). Committed; `--check` in `lint:strict` and `build` fails when stale. Never edit it. |
| `revit/titleblock.cs` | Builds the title block family (`<family>.rfa`): frame, row rules, field labels, static words. |
| `revit/project_template.cs` | Builds the project template (`<template_file>.rte`) from Revit's `default.rte`: strips sheets and views, purges, then loads the family and the `<type_prefix>*` text types. |
| `revit/fill_sheet.cs` | Creates or refreshes sheets on the active document and writes each sheet's values into the layout's boxes. Re-runnable: it replaces only the text notes it owns. |
| `revit/new_project.cs` | Test harness: a new project from the template, saved and activated. |
| `build.sh` | Runs the above. `./build.sh <pid>` builds the family + template; `./build.sh <pid> test` also issues sheet A-001 from `test/surf-ave.json`, exports the PDF and renders a PNG. `SHEET_PROPERTY=<p>` picks the property (default `bimcli`). |
| `test/render.py` | Renders the exported PDF to PNG (+ the strip) and asserts the media box (Arch D = 2592 x 1728 pt). |
| `test/surf-ave.json` | Sample per-sheet values (no layout path: `build.sh` adds it). |

Everything `build.sh` writes goes to `out/` (gitignored): `.rfa`, `.rte`, `.rvt`, `.pdf`, `.png` are build products,
never committed or published.

## Styles

| Style | Face | Ink | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wordmark` | serif 700 (Georgia Bold) | spot | the property's wordmark, the only spot-coloured text |
| `headline` | serif 700 | ink | project name |
| `label` | sans 600 (Segoe UI Semibold, bold off) | grey | field labels (kickers, uppercase) |
| `value` | sans 400 | ink | site, sheet name |
| `tagline` | sans 400 | grey | the line under the wordmark |
| `disclaimer` | sans 600 (Segoe UI Semibold, bold off) | ink | status / disclaimer words |
| `number` | sans 600 | ink | sheet number (not Georgia: its old-style figures read badly) |
| `url`, `data`, `figure` | mono 400 (Consolas) | ink | URL, data block, date, scale |

The kit tests (`test/sheet-template.test.mjs`) hold these rules: every colour is a light kit ink or the property's
spot, only the wordmark uses the spot, every style is one of the four faces, and the rows tile the strip.

## Build

```bash
pnpm --filter @bim-pdf/ui-kit gen                       # after editing sheet.json
bim revit launch --new --role reader --revit-version 2026   # a Revit of your own; note its pid
./build.sh <pid> test                                    # family + template + test sheet -> out/
```

A new property: add a block under `properties` in `sheet.json` (its name must have a DESIGN.md `spots:` entry), run
`gen`, and add the new `sheet.<property>.json` to `TEMPLATE_FILES` (scripts/publish.mjs) and the build.mjs list.

## Pitfalls

- **Keep per-sheet values ASCII.** A non-ASCII character (a middle dot) passed from bash through `--args-json`
  arrived mangled in Revit. Use plain hyphens and spaces in sample and real values.
- **Revit cannot create parameter-bound labels in a family from the API**, so values are text notes on the sheet,
  not title block parameters. Keep that design: re-running `fill_sheet.cs` is how a sheet is updated.
- **Purge before loading the title block** (a template has no sheets, so a loaded title block counts as unused).
  `project_template.cs` does it in that order.
- **`LoadFamily` returns null when the family is already loaded**; the scripts look the family up by name.
- **A semibold face is its own font family** (`Segoe UI Semibold`) with Revit's bold flag off; the bold flag would
  fake a heavier weight.
- **Verify the media box from the PDF**: the stock title blocks are not Arch D. `test/render.py` asserts it.
